steps.label: Costumes, Backdrops and Messages
steps.content:
Year 6 Scratch

Costumes, Backdrops and Messages

Year 6, 6.2.4

  • Animate a sprite by switching costumes in a loop.
  • Change level with a backdrop and a broadcast message.
  • Build an animation and a levels game that check themselves.

steps.label: Costumes Make Animation
steps.content:
Costumes Make Animation

A sprite can have several costumes. Swapping between them quickly makes it look alive.

  • next costume switches to the next one, and back to the first after the last.
  • Inside a loop with wait (0.2) seconds, the legs move at a walking pace.
  • set rotation style [left-right] keeps the sprite upright when it turns round.
when flag clicked
set rotation style [left-right v]
forever
move (6) steps
next costume
if on edge, bounce
wait (0.2) seconds
end

steps.label: Check: Costumes
steps.content:
Check: Costumes

A sprite has two costumes, walk1 and walk2.

items.prompt: The walk animation changes costume far too fast to see. Which block fixes it?
items.explain: A short wait inside the loop slows the costume changes down.

items.prompt: The sprite is wearing walk2. What does next costume do?
items.explain: After the last costume, next costume goes back to the first.

steps.label: Activity 1: Street Walker
steps.content:
Activity 1: Street Walker

Work on your own. Make the Walker walk up and down the street.

Build it

  • After the green flag the Walker keeps moving and switching costume.
  • The legs move at a walking pace.
  • At the edge it turns round and walks back, the right way up.

The panel beside TurboWarp lists the checks. Press Check my project as often as you like: it plays your game and tells you what it saw.

steps.label: Backdrops and Broadcasts
steps.content:
Backdrops and Broadcasts

A new level can be a new backdrop. A broadcast tells every sprite at once.

  • broadcast [level up] sends a message to every sprite and the stage.
  • Every when I receive [level up] script then starts, wherever it is.
  • switch backdrop to [Level 2] changes the stage picture.
  • One message can start many scripts: the backdrop changes, the Hero speaks, level becomes 2.
if <(score) = (5)> then
broadcast [level up v]
end

when I receive [level up v]
switch backdrop to [Level 2 v]
set [level v] to (2)

steps.label: Check: Messages
steps.content:
Check: Messages

Choose the best answer.

items.prompt: Which block starts a script when a message arrives?
items.explain: broadcast sends the message. when I receive waits for it.

items.prompt: Which scripts start when [level up] is broadcast?
options: Only scripts in the sprite that sent it
Every when I receive [level up] script
items.explain: A broadcast goes to every sprite and the stage.

steps.label: Activity 2: Level Up
steps.content:
Activity 2: Level Up

Work on your own. The Hero already moves with the arrow keys.

Build it

  • The green flag sets the backdrop to Level 1, score to 0 and level to 1.
  • Touching the Coin adds 1 to score and sends the Coin somewhere new.
  • At 5 coins, broadcast level up.
  • Receiving level up switches to Level 2, sets level to 2 and the Hero says Level 2!

The panel beside TurboWarp lists the checks. Press Check my project as often as you like: it plays your game and tells you what it saw.
